title: Windows devices receive too many attack surface reduction policies

maxPolicies.text: Attack surface reduction rule policies one device may receive before the set is hard to follow

report.title: {Items.Sum(i => i.DeviceCount)} Windows {Plural(Items.Sum(i => i.DeviceCount), 'device receives', 'devices receive')} more than {params.maxPolicies} attack surface reduction policies

messages.businessImpact: Some devices take their attack surface reduction rules from more than {params.maxPolicies} policies at once. Intune combines them, and a rule that two of those policies set differently is held back from the device altogether, so the more policies overlap, the more likely a protection is silently missing and the harder it is to say what any device enforces.
messages.technicalDetail: Counts, for each managed Windows device, the assigned attack surface reduction policies that configure at least one rule, and lists each distinct set of more than {params.maxPolicies}. Many policies across the tenant are not a finding: only policies that reach the same devices are counted together.
remediation: Consolidate the policies in each listed set into fewer policies, ideally one baseline set of rules for every device and a small number of exceptions.
Where a set is intended, check the policy's per-setting status in the Intune admin center for rules reported in conflict.
messages.cannotSee: Only endpoint security policies are counted, so rules delivered through a security baseline, an endpoint protection profile or a custom profile are not. A policy targeted at users, at a group whose members were not read, at a mixed group or through an assignment filter has unknown reach and is left out, so a device may receive more policies than counted, never fewer. Whether two policies actually set the same rule differently is not compared.
